source_name: EBA Register of payment and electronic money institutions under PSD2 (PIR)
why_relevant: Daily-updated, machine-readable central register of authorised PIs/EMIs/agents per member state, incl. CZ entities and passporting. Structural actor map of the CZ payments market (acquirers, PSPs, e-money issuers) with change history — a proxy for market entry/exit that no statistical series gives.

source_name: EBA Credit Institutions Register (CIR) and other lists of institutions (EUCLID)
why_relevant: Authoritative EU-wide list of authorised credit institutions incl. Czech banks and branches, sourced through EUCLID. Provides the denominator/actor list for CZ banking-sector coverage and lets CZ bank population be tracked consistently against other EU markets.

source_name: BIS Data Portal — CPMI payments and FMI (Red Book) statistics
why_relevant: Global harmonised Red Book statistics on LVPS/RPS/FPS, cards, terminals and cash, downloadable as country/comparative tables and CSV/SDMX. Valuable for placing CZ (once matched via ECB data) into a global rather than merely EU frame; note CZ is not a current CPMI member jurisdiction, so its role here is comparator-benchmarking rather than direct CZ coverage.

source_name: BIS Data Portal — CPMI CT: retail payments, currency and related indicators (cash trends)
why_relevant: Banknotes and coins in circulation, narrow money and retail payment indicators in comparable form — the standard reference for cash-usage trend analysis and cash-vs-card substitution narratives. Directly serves the 'cash usage' topic for benchmarking CZ against CPMI peers.

source_name: BIS CPMI — 'Payment systems in the Czech Republic' (Red Book country study, d25)
why_relevant: Dedicated BIS Red Book country monograph on the Czech payment system — the deepest supranational structural description of CZ clearing/settlement ever published by BIS. Historic (first CZ edition), so use as a baseline/definitional reference and for institutional lineage, not current figures.

source_name: IMF Financial Access Survey (FAS)
why_relevant: Annual supply-side financial-access indicators normalised per 100,000 adults / per 1,000 km² — ATMs, branches, POS terminals, card and mobile-money transactions — with Czechia reported. The canonical normalised ATM/branch density series for cross-country comparison, with longer and more stable definitions than national releases.

source_name: DBnomics mirror of IMF/FAS
why_relevant: Third-party open mirror of the IMF FAS series with a stable, well-documented API and series browser. Practical fallback when the IMF portal migration breaks endpoints, and convenient for discovering exact FAS series codes for Czechia.

source_name: FRED (St. Louis Fed) — IMF FAS-derived Czech Republic series
why_relevant: FRED republishes IMF FAS geographical-outreach and use-of-financial-services indicators as clean per-country time series (e.g. CZ commercial-bank branches, outstanding loans). Excellent low-friction API for charting and vintage tracking of CZ access indicators.

source_name: World Bank Open Data — ATMs per 100,000 adults (FB.ATM.TOTL.P5) and related WDI indicators
why_relevant: World Bank WDI re-publication of the IMF FAS ATM-density indicator with a very stable public API and full country panel — the easiest route to a consistent CZ ATM-density series with peer countries, and useful for detecting when the underlying FAS value was revised.

source_name: World Bank Global Findex Database 2025
why_relevant: The only globally comparable DEMAND-side source: ~300 indicators on account ownership, digital payments, card use, mobile/internet use, digital safety and financial resilience from nationally representative surveys of 141 economies incl. Czechia. Complements supply-side ECB/IMF terminal counts with consumer behaviour, incl. cash-vs-digital substitution.

source_name: World Bank Global Payment Systems Survey (GPSS)
why_relevant: Central-bank-answered global survey combining quantitative and qualitative measures of national payment-system development: infrastructure, legal/regulatory environment, retail instruments (cards and terminals), innovation, remittances and oversight. Gives institutional/regulatory context for CZ that pure statistics cannot, and reveals central-bank self-assessment.

source_name: Eurostat — E-banking and e-commerce dataset (isoc_bde15cbc) and ICT usage collections (isoc_i, isoc_e)
why_relevant: Harmonised EU survey data on internet banking and online purchasing by individuals and enterprises, with Czechia broken out and regional cuts available. The best supranational proxy for CZ digital-payment adoption behaviour and e-commerce demand driving card/POS volumes. Note isoc_bde15cbc itself is a legacy collection (last update 2019); current equivalents live in the isoc_i family.

source_name: ČSÚ — Mezinárodní data / Publikace obsahující mezinárodní srovnání (Czech NSI gateway to Eurostat & international databases)
why_relevant: The Czech statistical office's own curated index of the international databases it feeds and links to, in Czech. Snowball hub for discovering which supranational datasets carry CZ data and under what Czech-language labels — closes the cs-language gap around otherwise English-only supranational layers.

source_name: Knihovna VŠE — Přehled zdrojů pro statistiku (academic source guide, CZ)
why_relevant: Prague University of Economics library guide listing Czech and international statistical sources with Czech-language descriptions. A low-cost snowball hub that surfaces supranational and commercial databases a foreign researcher would otherwise miss, and supplies Czech terminology for further searching.

source_name: ECB Study on the payment attitudes of consumers in the euro area (SPACE)
why_relevant: The reference methodology and benchmark for POS cash-vs-card behaviour in Europe. Czechia is NOT covered (euro area only), so its value here is methodological (questionnaire design, definitions of POS/P2P shares) and as a comparator set against which any CZ national cash-usage survey must be read.

source_name: Euronet Services Czech Republic – euronetatms.cz (fees & network pages)
why_relevant: Largest independent ATM deployer (IAD) in CZ; its own site publishes fee structure (Direct Access Fee), network positioning and myth/fact pages that quantify its estate and rural expansion.

source_name: Euronet Worldwide Investor Relations / SEC EDGAR filings (10-K, quarterly)
why_relevant: Parent-level mandatory disclosure: ATM counts by segment (EFT Processing / Europe), transaction volumes, DCC and access-fee economics. Historic filings explicitly enumerate Czech ATM estate; recent filings give segment-level trends useful for sizing the IAD share.

source_name: ČNB – Peněžní oběh / Struktura peněz v oběhu (banknote & coin issuance)
why_relevant: Authoritative issuance data: number and value of banknotes/coins in circulation by denomination, updated regularly. Core denominator for any cash-usage trend argument.

source_name: Zákon č. 136/2011 Sb. o oběhu bankovek a mincí (full text on ČNB)
why_relevant: Legal frame that creates the cash-handling licensing regime, the obligation to accept cash, and the reporting duties of processors — explains why certain datasets exist and who must file them.

source_name: Loomis Czech Republic a.s. – corporate site (cash management services)
why_relevant: Major CIT/cash-processing operator in CZ; service pages describe processing volumes model, ČNB hand-off workflow and network of cash centres — qualitative structure of the cash supply chain.

source_name: Sbírka listin (Justice.cz obchodní rejstřík) – filed accounts of CIT/IAD entities
why_relevant: Statutory deposit of annual reports and financial statements for Loomis Czech Republic a.s. (IČO 26110709), Brink's Cash Solutions (CZ), G4S Secure Solutions (CZ), Euronet Services spol. s r.o. — the only quantified, audited view of CIT/IAD revenue, headcount and asset base in CZ.

source_name: Brink's Česká republika – brinks.cz (news, fleet and cash-management pages)
why_relevant: Publishes concrete operational metrics (fleet size, armoured-vehicle counts, cash-centre history) and announces structural moves such as the 2020 split from G4S and the 2025 G4S Secure Solutions partnership — direct evidence of CIT market consolidation.

source_name: G4S Česko – g4s.com/cs-cz (services, history, news)
why_relevant: Second CIT pillar; describes cash and valuables transport across CZ and to neighbouring EU states, and documents the 2020 corporate split that reshaped the CZ CIT market.

source_name: Sdružení pro bankovní karty (SBK) – bankovnikarty.cz statistics
why_relevant: Industry association publishing the canonical CZ series for ATM counts, ATM withdrawal value, POS terminals and — uniquely for this cell — cash-back at POS volumes. Historically the only public source quantifying cash-back.

source_name: SBK annual press release distributed via ČTK Protext / ČeskéNoviny
why_relevant: Full-text mirror of SBK's yearly sector release (card turnover vs ATM withdrawal value, e.g. CZK 1.784tn merchant volume vs CZK 853bn ATM withdrawals in 2024). Useful when the association's own site lags or paywalls detail.

source_name: Měšec.cz – cash-back and ATM-fee reporting
why_relevant: Consumer-finance outlet that regularly obtains and republishes bank-supplied cash-back counts and volumes, ATM fee changes and branch/cash-desk closures — often the earliest quantified public record before association statistics appear.

source_name: Peníze.cz – branch/cash-desk count tracker and cash-back series
why_relevant: Runs a recurring survey of Czech banks' branch and cash-desk (pokladny) counts, plus cash-back adoption pieces. Effectively the public substitute for a missing official branch-closure dataset.

source_name: Česká pošta – Poštovní výběr kartou (cash access at post offices) and Pošta Partner
why_relevant: Post-office network (~2,900 outlets incl. Pošta Partner) is the main non-bank cash-access substitute where branches and ATMs disappear; the card-withdrawal service (rollout counts, CZK 100–3,000 limits, fee) is a quantified cash-access datapoint tied to municipality-level coverage.
